concepts.description: Measure resolve rate with each ACI piece swapped or removed so human-UI instincts do not silently regress the agent harness.
concepts.title: ACI Component Ablation

concepts.description: Keep agent actions simple and efficient, feedback informative but concise, and add guardrails that catch common errors before they compound.
concepts.title: ACI Design Principles

concepts.description: Require one thought and one action per turn, repair or strip malformed replies, and stop the episode after repeated format failures.
concepts.title: Action Format Enforcement

concepts.description: Let the model decide when and what to retrieve mid-generation — paging external memory as a tool call rather than a single upfront top-K dump.
concepts.title: Active Retrieval During Generation

concepts.description: Frame a prompt as a conversation where one party asks for help and the other provides it, the document type ChatML itself is built around.
concepts.title: Advice Conversation Document

concepts.description: Design the commands, observations, and history formatting an LM agent uses to operate a computer so digital work matches model limits, not human GUIs.
concepts.title: Agent-Computer Interface

concepts.description: The order planned actions execute — sequential, parallel, conditional, or looped — with the model itself often determining non-sequential branches.
concepts.title: Agent Control Flow

concepts.description: Turn millions of raw trajectory tokens into a navigable, per-task root-cause report plus a single benchmark-level overview, so a downstream agent can act on evidence without reading every trace.
concepts.title: Agent Debugger Trajectory Distillation

concepts.description: Represent places and objects as a containment tree rendered to natural language, with each agent holding only a personal subgraph that can go stale.
concepts.title: Agent Environment Tree

concepts.description: Compose an agent episode as fixed system, optional demonstration, instance brief, then per-turn next-step templates around action and observation.
concepts.title: Agent Episode Prompt Stack

concepts.description: Distinguish intentional submit, cost-limit submit, cost-limit with no edits, and early format-exit — only intentional submits resolve at useful rates.
concepts.title: Agent Episode Termination Modes

concepts.description: A trial's transcript is what the agent claims happened; its outcome is the actual resulting environment state — grade the outcome, since a transcript can narrate success that never occurred.
concepts.title: Agent Eval Outcome vs Transcript

concepts.description: Code-based, model-based, and human graders trade objectivity and cost against nuance and scale — choose the grader type the check actually needs, not whichever is easiest to wire up.
concepts.title: Agent Grader Types

concepts.description: Internal model knowledge, short-term context, and long-term external stores form a hierarchy for what an agent retains and where.
concepts.title: Agent Memory Tiers

concepts.description: Plans fail via invalid tools, bad parameters, wrong values, unmet goals or constraints, or false success from broken reflection.
concepts.title: Agent Planning Failure Modes

concepts.description: Isolation, approval gates, scope filters, and input/output guardrails that contain damage when prompt defenses fail on a tool-using agent.
concepts.title: Agent System-Level Defenses

concepts.description: Agent tools fall into knowledge augmentation, capability extension, and write actions, with risk rising sharply for tools that mutate the environment.
concepts.title: Agent Tool Categories

concepts.description: The right tool can still return wrong output, mistranslate an NL plan, or be missing entirely — failures that must be tested per tool, not only per plan.
concepts.title: Agent Tool Failure Modes

concepts.description: Expect early localization/reproduction, then mid-episode edit–evaluate cycles, then submit — and redesign recovery when the first approach fails.
concepts.title: Agent Trajectory Phases

concepts.description: UI controls that expose tool activity, let users edit or authorize calls, and regenerate from a corrected point so humans steer the agent mid-trajectory.
concepts.title: Agent UX Steering Affordances

concepts.description: Declare models, data sources, and tools, then chain them so formats match and failures surface across multi-step agent and RAG pipelines.
concepts.title: AI Pipeline Orchestration

concepts.description: Responsible AI use costs verification time, but perceived productivity rewards skipping scrutiny — design harness gates that keep review mandatory.
concepts.title: AI Productivity Paradox

concepts.description: Frame a prompt as an analytical report — introduction through conclusion — when the task is objective analysis rather than conversation.
concepts.title: Analytic Report Document

concepts.description: Few-shot examples set an expectation that skews completions toward the examples' implied distribution, whether or not that was intended.
concepts.title: Anchoring Bias in Examples

concepts.description: Deterministically parse the model’s free-form extraction into a canonical answer type — number, choice letter, yes/no, or stripped free text.
concepts.title: Answer Cleansing

concepts.description: Score any foundation-model application against four buckets — domain capability, generation quality, instruction-following, and cost/latency — rather than a single vague "quality" number.
concepts.title: Application Evaluation Criteria

concepts.description: A model may invent plausible-looking placeholder values for tool arguments never mentioned in the conversation, producing schema-valid but semantically wrong calls, rather than asking for them.
concepts.title: Argument Hallucination

concepts.description: Two-role micro-workflow where a tool-using Assistant acts and a UserProxy keeps it on the human goal, corrects drift, and declares completion.
concepts.title: Assistant–UserProxy Pair

concepts.description: Turn recurring failed trajectory patterns into ACI changes automatically — tips, command docs, guardrails — instead of only hand-editing the interface.
concepts.title: Automated ACI Iteration

concepts.description: Classify automated agent-improvement methods by what evidence the optimizer observes and what surface it is allowed to edit, to see where full-harness evolution sits relative to single-surface methods.
concepts.title: Automated Agent Optimization Taxonomy

concepts.description: A model produces one committed token at a time with no ability to pause, backtrack, or edit — any correction has to be engineered on top, not expected from the raw generation process.
concepts.title: Autoregressive Generation

concepts.description: Test both cases where a behavior should occur and cases where it shouldn't — a one-sided eval only rewards one-sided optimization.
concepts.title: Balanced Eval Problem Sets

concepts.description: Decide separately from topology whether a workflow processes a known finite set of work items together or an ongoing stream as items arrive.
concepts.title: Batch vs. Streaming Workflow Processing

concepts.description: After finding a large file, repeatedly scrolling without search/goto wastes the episode — re-invoke search for the next symbol instead of linear hunting.
concepts.title: Blind Scroll Loop

concepts.description: Cap and normalize search-tool output so localization stays informative without drowning the context window in unbounded grep dumps.
concepts.title: Bounded Search Observations

concepts.description: Spawn N independent solver trajectories on the same problem, then merge their outputs with a dedicated agent into a stronger combined solution.
concepts.title: Branch-Solve-Merge

concepts.description: Prefer task-agnostic prompts that elicit broad reasoning skills when you need one template across tasks; reserve narrow per-task templates for format-heavy niches.
concepts.title: Broad vs Narrow Prompting

concepts.description: Separate a browsing phase that gathers quoted references from a later answer phase that composes only from those references and the question.
concepts.title: Browse-Then-Answer Episode

concepts.description: Give browsing agents a small closed command set — search, click-by-ID, find, quote, scroll, back, end — instead of free-form browser scripting.
concepts.title: Browser Tool Action Inventory

concepts.description: Two ways to define a test "example" for a multi-call conversational loop — replay a scripted transcript, or have a model play the user's side too.
concepts.title: Canned Conversations and Model-Mocked User

concepts.description: Capability evals should start hard and pass rarely, to give a target to climb toward; regression evals should pass almost always, so any drop is a signal something broke.
concepts.title: Capability vs Regression Evals

concepts.description: Eliciting step-by-step natural-language reasoning before the final answer measurably improves multi-step task accuracy, because emitting the reasoning as visible text is the only way a model can build on its own intermediate insight.
concepts.title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting

concepts.description: Chat models buy unambiguous turn-taking and instruction compliance at the cost of alignment tax, excess chattiness, and loss of expressive range.
concepts.title: Chat vs. Completion Tradeoffs

concepts.description: A markup language tagging conversation turns with roles — system, user, assistant — that chat models are fine-tuned to complete unambiguously.
concepts.title: ChatML Format

concepts.description: Reserved role-marker tokens can't be produced by ordinary user text, so an API caller is structurally confined to the user role and cannot fake turns.
concepts.title: ChatML Injection Resistance

concepts.description: A model tends to treat any retrieved snippet as meaningfully relevant and feels compelled to use it, so irrelevant hits actively mislead the answer.
concepts.title: Chekhov's Gun Retrieval Fallacy

concepts.description: Split sources into indexable units with size, overlap, and split rules that trade retrieval diversity against boundary integrity and index cost.
concepts.title: Chunking Strategy

concepts.description: Require agents to collect quotable references while using tools so answers are checkable for factual accuracy without independent research.
concepts.title: Citation-Backed Agent Answers

concepts.description: When issue text is tiny and repos are huge, BM25 file retrieval underperforms interactive localization — and stuffing more retrieved tokens often hurts.
concepts.title: Codebase Retrieval for Agents

concepts.description: Coding agents grade naturally against deterministic test pass/fail signals, with transcript-level heuristics and rubrics layered on top for quality beyond correctness.
concepts.title: Coding Agent Eval Design

concepts.description: Preserve history structure while replacing old tool or command outputs with short placeholders to cut tokens and drop stale duplicate state.
concepts.title: Collapsed Observations

concepts.description: Choose start and end cues so the harness can extract the main answer — prefer formats whose end-test is a simple substring when possible.
concepts.title: Completion Boundary Markers

concepts.description: Average a completion's token logprobs into a confidence signal that can drive application behavior, without treating it as an absolute quality score.
concepts.title: Completion Confidence Scoring

concepts.description: A completion's leading text is boilerplate, reasoning, or fluff — only one of which is worth paying tokens for, and each needs a different fix.
concepts.title: Completion Preamble Types

concepts.description: Engineer how and where a completion-model generation halts, since nothing in the API tells a completion model a turn has naturally ended.
concepts.title: Completion Stop-Condition Design

concepts.description: Isolate one evolved harness component at a time to see where an evolution loop's gain actually lives — components own different failure surfaces and interact non-additively, capping the aggregate improvement.
concepts.title: Component-Level Harness Ablation

concepts.description: Expose every editable harness piece as its own file at a fixed mount point so each failure pattern localizes to one component and every edit is a reviewable, revertible diff.
concepts.title: Component Observability

concepts.description: Teach solve-stage few-shots to name component outputs and how they concatenate or repeat, so composition reuses simpler meanings instead of flat I/O pairs.
concepts.title: Compositional Mapping Exemplars

concepts.description: Under least-to-most on compositional commands, failures split into bad decompositions versus translation bugs — modifiers, conjunction order, copies.
concepts.title: Compositional Translation Failure Modes

concepts.description: Treat multi-component LLM systems as optimizable computation graphs so prompts, solutions, and tools improve via automated feedback—not only craft.
concepts.title: Compound AI System Optimization

concepts.description: Per-step accuracy multiplies across a multi-step agent trajectory, so long plans fail even when each individual step looks reliable.
concepts.title: Compound Mistake Amplification

concepts.description: Verify a computer-use agent by inspecting real backend and application state after the fact, not the on-screen confirmation alone, and account for its DOM-versus-screenshot interaction trade-off.
concepts.title: Computer-Use Agent Eval State Checks

concepts.description: Specify an agent-computer interface as config — prompt templates, command files, parsers, history processors, and stateful environment variables.
concepts.title: Configurable ACI Harness

concepts.description: Use the fraction of sampled paths that agree with the majority answer as a cheap calibration cue — low agreement means the model may not know.
concepts.title: Consistency as Uncertainty Signal

concepts.description: Classify context by how directly it comes from the user — their own words, indirect nearby sources, or boilerplate that only shapes the response.
concepts.title: Context Directness Spectrum

concepts.description: Deliberate structuring of instructions, examples, retrieved material, and working memory inside the context window for reliable model behaviour.
concepts.title: Context Engineering

concepts.description: How urgently a request needs a response bounds how context can be gathered for it — and drives how much of that context should be prepared in advance.
concepts.title: Context Gathering Latency Tiers

concepts.description: Supply the information the model needs in-prompt, and when required restrict answers to that context so parametric knowledge cannot leak through.
concepts.title: Context Grounding

concepts.description: Vary the target question's individual words and aspects to surface what context would help answer it, before checking what's actually obtainable.
concepts.title: Context Mind Mapping

concepts.description: Sort candidate context sources by how close they are to the application and how often they change, since both predict how hard they are to use.
concepts.title: Context Source Proximity and Stability

concepts.description: Prepend metadata or model-generated situating text to each chunk before indexing so retrieval works when the chunk alone lacks standalone meaning.
concepts.title: Contextual Chunk Augmentation

concepts.description: Structured data attached to transcript messages — UI selections, documents, or tool-derived lists — so the agent sees task context without copy/paste.
concepts.title: Conversation Artifacts

concepts.description: Assemble preamble, prior conversation, and the current exchange — including tool call/response traces — into the transcript the agent sees each turn.
concepts.title: Conversational Agent Context

concepts.description: Grading a conversational agent needs a second LLM playing the user, because the quality of the interaction itself — not just the end state — is part of what's being measured.
concepts.title: Conversational Agent Eval Simulation

concepts.description: Conversational agents lack a built-in mechanism for processing discrete work units and no enforceable lever over how a task gets done, unlike a workflow.
concepts.title: Conversational Agent Structural Limitations

concepts.description: Categorize wrong chain-of-thought traces — logical mistakes, calculator errors, unnecessary steps, prior-knowledge gaps, or never starting to reason.
concepts.title: CoT Failure Modes

concepts.description: Use natural-language chain-of-thought to map instructions onto discrete action sequences when the hard part is choosing and ordering grounded steps.
concepts.title: CoT for Action Grounding

concepts.description: With sufficient scale, chain-of-thought exemplars of short chains can transfer to longer out-of-distribution step counts where standard prompting fails.
concepts.title: CoT Length Generalization

concepts.description: A correct final answer does not imply a correct reasoning path — treat CoT traces as debugging evidence, not as verified proofs of intermediate steps.
concepts.title: CoT Path Correctness Gap

concepts.description: Requesting logprobs on the prompt itself, not just the completion, surfaces surprising, anomalous, or high-information-density passages in the input.
concepts.title: Critical Point Detection via Logprobs

concepts.description: Keep the feedback engine to criticism only; let a separate optimizer step propose the next variable value — do not conflate diagnose and rewrite.
concepts.title: Critique–Optimizer Separation

concepts.description: Few-shot CoT exemplars from another domain help mainly when answer format matches; mismatched formats collapse gains — often worse than zero-shot CoT.
concepts.title: Cross-Task Few-Shot CoT Transfer

concepts.description: Route a failed work item back to an earlier task for another attempt, at the cost of context reattachment, universal failure handling, and loop limits.
concepts.title: Cyclic Workflow Repair Loops

concepts.description: Least-to-most fails when subquestions are nonsensical or when a sub-answer is wrong; CoT often fails earlier by picking the wrong fact or operator.
concepts.title: Decomposition Before Composition Failures

concepts.description: Probe long-conversation consistency with questions answerable only from prior sessions — favoring full recall plus paginated search over lossy summary baselines.
concepts.title: Deep Memory Retrieval

concepts.description: Design system prompts and input handling so untrusted user content cannot override developer instructions or exfiltrate privileged context.
concepts.title: Defensive Prompt Engineering

concepts.description: Pay for tree search over thoughts only when CoT already fails — knobs like beam size, votes, and mixed generate/evaluate models buy performance at 5–100× token cost.
concepts.title: Deliberate Search Cost Tradeoff

concepts.description: Predict a completion by imagining a random training-set document that happens to start with the prompt, not by asking how a reasonable person would reply.
concepts.title: Document-Completion Prediction Heuristic

concepts.description: Measure whether a model understands the subject matter at all — usually via domain benchmarks — without mistaking multiple-choice discrimination for open-ended generation skill.
concepts.title: Domain-Capability Evaluation

concepts.description: Decomposition few-shots rarely transfer across domains — invest in within-domain demos because a correct split usually decides success.
concepts.title: Domain-Specific Decomposition Prompts

concepts.description: Editing a function without knowing what else in the codebase depends on its current behavior can silently corrupt callers instead of only under-fixing.
concepts.title: Downstream Dependent Blind Spot

concepts.description: A teleprompter compiles a DSPy program through candidate generation, parameter selection, and optional program-structure search — discrete stages, not a single optimization pass.
concepts.title: DSPy Compiler Three Stages

concepts.description: Wrap a signature in a callable module whose LM choice, instructions, and demonstrations are explicit parameters a compiler can search over, so published prompting techniques become swappable, signature-agnostic components.
concepts.title: DSPy Module Parameterization

concepts.description: Declare what a text transformation needs to do — typed input/output field names, not a hand-written prompt string — so a compiler can generate and refine the actual prompting strategy.
concepts.title: DSPy Signature Abstraction

concepts.description: Compile an expensive teacher program first, then bootstrap a cheap student program's demonstrations or finetuning data from the teacher's own traces — even when no labels exist for the student's intermediate steps.
concepts.title: DSPy Teacher-Program Distillation

concepts.description: Runtime collection of per-instance background under latency, preparability, and comparability constraints — usually the bulk of context-design work.
concepts.title: Dynamic Context Gathering

concepts.description: Find what runtime context to gather by mind-mapping the question and ranking sources by application proximity and stability.
concepts.title: Dynamic Context Source Discovery

concepts.description: Let users edit a shown tool call's arguments and resubmit, regenerating the conversation forward from that corrected point.
concepts.title: Editable Tool-Call Correction

concepts.description: Represent one piece of retrieved content at several sizes so prompt assembly can fit the largest version the remaining budget allows.
concepts.title: Elastic Snippets

concepts.description: Filter candidate memory connections cheaply with embedding similarity, then let an LLM judge which of those candidates are genuinely related — neither step alone finds good links at scale.
concepts.title: Embedding-Plus-LLM Memory Linking

concepts.description: Believable group behaviors — information diffusion, relationship continuity, and event coordination — arise from per-agent memory and planning, not hard-coded scripts.
concepts.title: Emergent Multi-Agent Coordination

concepts.description: Judge harness changes on episode outcomes, trajectory phases, and budgets — not on sub-second per-tool-call latency habits borrowed from request APM.
concepts.title: Episode-Scale Evaluation vs Request-Scale APM

concepts.description: Store a small buffer of self-reflection texts across trials so later trajectories see distilled lessons, not only the latest raw trace.
concepts.title: Episodic Reflection Memory

concepts.description: Define evaluation criteria before building (or before a capability exists), so shipped features stay measurable and future-model bets become trackable instead of wishful.
concepts.title: Eval-Driven Development

concepts.description: Start every eval trial from a clean environment — shared state between trials creates correlated failures that look like agent performance and can let an agent cheat on leftovers from a previous run.
concepts.title: Eval Environment Isolation

concepts.description: Censor environment observations that overlap the question or reference answer so agents cannot solve the eval by copying leaked gold text.
concepts.title: Eval Observation Anti-Leakage

concepts.description: Three ways to find enough example problems for evaluation at scale — mine existing records, harvest app usage, or generate samples with an LLM.
concepts.title: Eval Sample Sourcing

concepts.description: A capability eval near 100% pass rate has stopped giving improvement signal, and near-saturation score deltas understate real capability gains because only the hardest remaining tasks can still move the number.
concepts.title: Eval Saturation

concepts.description: A shared eval suite resolves spec ambiguity between people up front and becomes the highest-bandwidth channel through which a product team hands research or engineering a concrete target to optimize against.
concepts.title: Eval Suite As Product-Research Interface

concepts.description: Test a single model pass or the whole application loop depending on what changed — unit-test isolated prompts, regression-test architecture changes.
concepts.title: Eval Test Granularity

concepts.description: Attach every harness edit to a self-declared, falsifiable prediction of what it will fix and what it might break, then verify that prediction against the next round's real outcomes.
concepts.title: Evidence-Driven Change Manifest

concepts.description: A minimal offline-eval starting point — a handful of example inputs run through the app, with results eyeballed by hand rather than auto-scored.
concepts.title: Example Suite

concepts.description: Tell document agents the answer is always in archival memory and to keep searching — including nested key lookups — until verification, not early exit.
concepts.title: Exhaustive Archival Search Instruction

concepts.description: Ambiguity-free task wording, personas, examples, and explicit output formats that tell the model exactly what success looks like.
concepts.title: Explicit Instruction Design

concepts.description: Post-process equations inside a chain of thought with a deterministic calculator so correct plans are not failed by arithmetic slips.
concepts.title: External Calculator for CoT

concepts.description: Check whether generated claims are supported by a scoped context (local) or by world knowledge (global), using judges, self-consistency, search augmentation, or textual entailment — not fluency alone.
concepts.title: Factual Consistency Evaluation

concepts.description: Encode recurring failed strategies seen in development trajectories as short imperative tips in the instance prompt to steer later episodes.
concepts.title: Failure-Derived Prompt Tips

concepts.description: Present few-shot examples either explicitly labeled as examples, or folded in as previously solved tasks the model believes it already completed.
concepts.title: Few-Shot Example Formatting

concepts.description: Drop the oldest short-term messages first when the window fills — simple, but often deletes the purpose-setting turns that matter most.
concepts.title: FIFO Context Eviction

concepts.description: Full fine-tuning, LoRA, and soft prompting trade training-document volume and duration against how much genuinely new behavior they can teach.
concepts.title: Fine-Tuning Approach Comparison

concepts.description: Treat fine-tuning as baking static instructions and few-shots into weights so prompts shrink — LoRA for format and priors, full FT for new domains.
concepts.title: Fine-Tuning as Prompt Continuation

concepts.description: Decide whether to fine-tune based on whether you can gather enough correct, well-formatted, on-domain training examples — not on model quality alone.
concepts.title: Fine-Tuning Decision

concepts.description: Disable tool choice for a turn while still declaring tools so the model must plan in language before it is allowed to call functions.
concepts.title: Forced Reasoning Before Tools

concepts.description: Extract structured content from free-form input by defining a tool shaped like the target structure and forcing the model to call it.
concepts.title: Forced Tool-Choice Extraction

concepts.description: Rebuild each agent turn from a written environment summary so the only memory of prior steps is what the harness deliberately records.
concepts.title: Fresh-Context State Summary

concepts.description: Let the model request immediate follow-up inference after a tool result so multi-step retrieval or edits can run without waiting for a new user turn.
concepts.title: Function-Call Chaining

concepts.description: Model-provider-native tool use — declare a tool inventory, let the model emit structured calls, execute them in the harness, and feed results back.
concepts.title: Function Calling

concepts.description: When gold answers are absent, score whether the completion works — parseable, valid tool calls, or passing existing unit tests.
concepts.title: Functional Completion Testing

concepts.description: Small prompt or model changes produce unforeseeable behavioural shifts, so agent harnesses need continuous offline regression—not one-time validation.
concepts.title: GenAI Radical Fragility

concepts.description: Rank GenAI collaboration from checking your work up through independent complex problem-solving — autonomy rises with risk and oracle demand.
concepts.title: GenAI Use Safety Modes

concepts.description: Today's LLMs trade generality (working across any domain) against strength (reliably solving complex tasks); narrowing scope is how you buy the latter.
concepts.title: Generality–Strength Tradeoff

concepts.description: For strong models, de-emphasize fluency and coherence checks and invest evaluation budget in factual consistency and safety — the generation failures that still ship as user-visible harm.
concepts.title: Generation-Capability Evaluation

concepts.description: Prefer generative readers when answers need synthesis across clue-bearing passages or parametric fallback — extractive spans score zero if the string never appears.
concepts.title: Generation Over Extractive Retrieval

concepts.description: Once a repetitive pattern starts by chance, continuing it is statistically more likely at every subsequent step than breaking it, since the model has no mechanism for getting bored.
concepts.title: Generation Repetition Trap

concepts.description: Condition long-horizon agent behavior on a memory stream, recursive reflection, and hierarchical plans rather than single-shot LM prompts.
concepts.title: Generative Agent Architecture

concepts.description: Score a completion by comparing it against a trusted reference solution, matching on one carefully chosen aspect rather than the whole output.
concepts.title: Gold-Standard Matching

concepts.description: A low agent score can mean the grader is broken, not the agent — check the grader before concluding capability is lacking, and design it so passing requires actually solving the task rather than exploiting a loophole.
concepts.title: Grader Correctness as Eval Hygiene

concepts.description: Decide up front whether a task passes when every grader agrees or when a weighted blend clears a threshold — the combination rule changes what "passing" actually means as much as the graders themselves do.
concepts.title: Grader Score Combination

concepts.description: Add elements highest-value-first or remove them lowest-value-first to fit the token budget, choosing direction based on how elements interact.
concepts.title: Greedy Prompt Assembly

concepts.description: Validate an LLM-as-judge pipeline by checking it doesn't widen disagreement beyond what a pool of human assessors already disagrees on among themselves.
concepts.title: Grounding LLM Assessment in Human Evaluation

concepts.description: Apply multi-line edits only when lint or syntax checks pass; on failure revert and show error type, proposed snippet, and original content.
concepts.title: Guardrailed Edit Tool

concepts.description: A model cannot internally distinguish a recalled fact from a plausible invention, so confident-sounding fabrication is a structural property of generation, not an occasional bug.
concepts.title: Hallucination

concepts.description: Holding the base model fixed, harness design alone materially shifts task completion — and the best harness is model-specific, so it must be re-adapted every time the base model changes.
concepts.title: Harness as a Performance Lever

concepts.description: Match a harness fix to the component level whose enforcement strength and scope fits the failure — and if a level doesn't stick after repeated attempts, pivot to a different level rather than iterating harder there.
concepts.title: Harness Component-Level Selection

concepts.description: Prompt templates, user behaviour, and silent provider model swaps all change agent behaviour without code diffs — version and detect them as first-class maintenance risks.
concepts.title: Harness Drift Awareness

concepts.description: The rollout-attribute-distill-edit-commit cycle that drives automatic harness evolution one iteration at a time, with multiple rollouts per task so partial-pass signal survives into diagnosis.
concepts.title: Harness Evolution Outer Loop

concepts.description: Freeze an evolved harness and move it to an unseen benchmark or a different base model without further evolution — the result separates general engineering experience from benchmark-specific tuning.
concepts.title: Harness Evolution Transfer and Generalization

concepts.description: An evolve loop's self-declared fix predictions land far above chance, but its regression predictions barely beat chance — it can justify why an edit helps but not reliably foresee what it will break.
concepts.title: Harness Self-Attribution's Regression Blindness

concepts.description: Generate a high-level plan first, then expand each step into a detailed sub-plan, avoiding the generate-hard versus execute-hard granularity bind.
concepts.title: Hierarchical Planning

concepts.description: Summarize a corpus too large for the context window by dividing it into window-sized units, summarizing each, then recursively summarizing the summaries along natural structure.
concepts.title: Hierarchical Summarization

concepts.description: Explicit per-action automation levels so humans can supply plans, validate them, or approve irreversible tool calls before the agent proceeds.
concepts.title: Human Approval Gates

concepts.description: Collect demonstrations through the same action/observation surface the model will use, exposing only deliberate exceptions such as memory summaries.
concepts.title: Human–Model Demo Interface Parity

concepts.description: Combine term-based and embedding-based retrieval — sequentially via reranking or in parallel via rank fusion — to catch both keywords and semantics.
concepts.title: Hybrid Retrieval

concepts.description: Prefer the smallest framework hook that fixes the bug over reimplementing larger APIs — agents often localize correctly then over-build the edit.
concepts.title: Idiomatic Minimal Patch Preference

concepts.description: Teaching desired behaviour from examples inside the prompt alone, without weight updates — zero-shot through N-shot adaptation at inference time.
concepts.title: In-Context Learning

concepts.description: Malicious instructions planted in tool outputs or retrieved documents that the agent treats as trusted commands once they enter context.
concepts.title: Indirect Prompt Injection

concepts.description: When computing an eval's pass rate, score a trial that dies on an infrastructure exception as a failure rather than discarding it, so the metric can't be inflated by silently dropping hard trials.
concepts.title: Count Infrastructure Failures As Task Failures

concepts.description: Decode until the model emits a call-result delimiter, pause generation, inject the tool response, then continue decoding in the same sequence.
concepts.title: Inline API Call Interruption

concepts.description: Harness checks on prompts and generations that block leaks, attacks, and bad outputs — with explicit policies per failure mode and false-refusal awareness.
concepts.title: Input Output Guardrails

concepts.description: Optimize one test-time solution for a single query, or optimize a prompt that must generalize across many queries — different variables, same feedback loop.
concepts.title: Instance vs Prompt Optimization

concepts.description: Measure whether the model obeys your stated constraints — format, length, vocabulary, style, content limits — separately from domain skill or prose quality, and build custom suites for the instructions your product actually uses.
concepts.title: Instruction-Following Evaluation

concepts.description: Train and design so conflicting instructions resolve toward higher-privilege layers — system over user over model output over tool output.
concepts.title: Instruction Hierarchy

concepts.description: Instruction-only optimizers rewrite system prompts; demonstration bootstrappers add few-shot traces — complementary levers that can be combined.
concepts.title: Instruction vs Demonstration Optimization

concepts.description: Classify what the user is trying to do so the agent selects the right tools and can decline out-of-scope queries before wasting a plan.
concepts.title: Intent Classification for Routing

concepts.description: Fall back between retrieval-grounded acting and sample-and-vote CoT when step budget or answer confidence shows one path is stuck.
concepts.title: Internal External Knowledge Routing

concepts.description: Count malformed or unknown commands against the episode action budget even when they are ignored, so format failure cannot be free.
concepts.title: Invalid Action Budget Accounting

concepts.description: Prefer searches that quote symbols and patterns from the issue text early — speculative filenames burn budget before the agent ever reaches the fix site.
concepts.title: Issue-Grounded Localization

concepts.description: Generate a search query from accumulated context at each of a fixed number of hops, retrieving more passages each time, before answering — a scripted alternative to letting an agent decide when to stop searching.
concepts.title: Iterative Multi-Hop Retrieval

concepts.description: Estimate each segment's token perplexity conditioned on the already- compressed version of prior segments, not the full original text, so earlier compression decisions correctly influence later ones.
concepts.title: Iterative Token-Level Compression

concepts.description: Subverting safety features or injecting malicious instructions so the model follows attacker goals instead of developer policy.
concepts.title: Jailbreaking and Prompt Injection

concepts.description: When assembled context still doesn't fit the token budget, shrink what's already selected — elide less-relevant lines or summarize — rather than dropping snippets outright.
concepts.title: Last-Minute Context Trimming

concepts.description: Decompose a hard problem into simpler subproblems and solve them in order, feeding each answer into the next prompt for easy-to-hard generalization.
concepts.title: Least-to-Most Prompting

concepts.description: Score retrieval candidates by literal word overlap with the query, after stripping stop words and stemming, as a fast proxy for relevance.
concepts.title: Lexical Similarity Scoring

concepts.description: Don't stray far from documents resembling the model's training data — the closer a prompt matches a familiar document type, the more stable the output.
concepts.title: Little Red Riding Hood Principle

concepts.description: An LLM agent is a model that perceives an environment and acts on it through a tool inventory, with the model itself serving as the planner.
concepts.title: LLM Agent

concepts.description: Convert a user's problem into a model-ready prompt in four steps — retrieve context, snippetize it, score and prioritize it, then assemble the prompt.
concepts.title: LLM Application Feedforward Pass

concepts.description: An LLM application is a transformation layer converting a user's problem into a document the model completes, then converting the completion back.
concepts.title: LLM Application Loop

concepts.description: Escalating autonomy where an LLM chooses, generates, or prioritizes tasks instead of a fixed DAG — trading dependability for open-ended flexibility.
concepts.title: LLM-Driven Workflow Routing

concepts.description: Rank candidate models by intelligence, speed, cost, ease of use, functionality, and special constraints — and keep the choice swappable in code.
concepts.title: LLM Model Selection Criteria

concepts.description: An LLM judging its own model family's output grades less accurately unless it's framed as reviewing a third party's work, not its own.
concepts.title: LLM Self-Assessment Grading Bias

concepts.description: Convert pages and search hits into tokenizer-stable text with numbered links, readability extracts, and media placeholders shaped for LM agents—not browsers.
concepts.title: LM-Oriented Web Observations

concepts.description: "How do models compare on this benchmark" is underspecified for LM pipelines — report accuracy against a fixed program and compiling/ optimization strategy so the comparison is reproducible.
concepts.title: Compare (Model, Program, Strategy) Triples, Not Models Alone

concepts.description: Use the language model itself to score or vote on frontier states so search can prune, look ahead, or backtrack without a hand-coded heuristic.
concepts.title: LM Search Heuristic

concepts.description: Shift a classifier's per-token logprobs by a constant to match the confidence threshold the application actually needs, not the model's default.
concepts.title: Logprob Classification Calibration

concepts.description: Use average token logprobs (or early-token probabilities) as a relative confidence signal to gate show/warn/retry/escalate decisions in the harness.
concepts.title: Logprob Completion Quality Signal

concepts.description: A model computes a full probability distribution over the next token, not just the one it picks, and can return those log-probabilities at no extra cost.
concepts.title: Logprobs Fundamentals

concepts.description: Long-context performance follows a U-curve: primacy and recency beat the middle, and longer windows do not by themselves fix position sensitivity.
concepts.title: Lost in the Middle

concepts.description: Split prompt tokens into read-only system instructions, a fixed working context block, and a FIFO message queue headed by a recursive summary.
concepts.title: Main-Context Sections

concepts.description: Form your own answer before consulting the model, start with oversimplified prompts, and review outputs with distrust heuristics to avoid anchoring.
concepts.title: Me-First Prompt Collaboration

concepts.description: Build long-memory eval questions that require the old conversation log — never answerable from persona summaries alone — so retrieval, not priors, is tested.
concepts.title: Memory Challenge Question Design

concepts.description: When a new memory links to existing neighbors, let those neighbors' own context, tags, and connections update in response, so the memory graph gets richer rather than merely bigger.
concepts.title: Memory Evolution on Retrieval

concepts.description: Adversarial conversation that implants false past events into an agent’s durable memory — a retrieval/reflection risk beyond ordinary prompt injection.
concepts.title: Memory Hacking

concepts.description: Decide what enters short-term context versus long-term store, and when to add, merge, summarize, or evict so the window stays within budget.
concepts.title: Memory Management

concepts.description: Warn the model before the window fills, then flush oldest in-context messages into durable recall while rebuilding a recursive summary.
concepts.title: Memory Pressure Eviction

concepts.description: Store natural-language experience records scored by recency, importance, and relevance so retrieval packs the most useful memories into context.
concepts.title: Memory Stream

concepts.description: Compress redundant short-term history into running summaries, merges, or reflection-driven updates to free context without discarding task state.
concepts.title: Memory Summarization

concepts.description: Fill the token budget from the end of the content backward, keeping the most recent elements with no scoring or prioritization needed.
concepts.title: Minimal Prompt Crafter

concepts.description: Start an automatic harness-evolution loop from a deliberately minimal seed so every component the loop adds must earn its place against measured rollouts, not inherit unattributed credit from hand-tuning.
concepts.title: Minimal Seed Harness

concepts.description: A unified interface to self-hosted and commercial models that centralizes access control, fallbacks, logging hooks, and API-change maintenance.
concepts.title: Model Gateway

concepts.description: Classify intent and send each query to the right model, human, FAQ, or tool path so simple work stays cheap and out-of-scope work is declined early.
concepts.title: Model Router

concepts.description: Choosing a model for a task balances output quality against cost, latency tolerance, and whether the base model's knowledge or behavior needs changing.
concepts.title: Model Selection Tradeoffs

concepts.description: Split agent work across specialized roles — planner, validator, executor, critic — so each component has a narrower job than a single monolithic agent.
concepts.title: Multi-Agent Architecture

concepts.description: Treat images and video in a prompt the same way as any other context — include only what's relevant, introduce their role in text, and favor familiar visual motifs over novel ones.
concepts.title: Multimodal Prompt Framing

concepts.description: Express agent plans in natural language then translate to tool calls, which is more robust to API churn than planning directly in exact function names.
concepts.title: Natural Language Action Plans

concepts.description: Extra tokens or post-answer rationales are not enough — useful CoT needs natural-language steps before the answer, not only equations or padding.
concepts.title: Natural-Language Intermediate Reasoning

concepts.description: Append hard format or domain rules as natural-language constraint blocks to the textual optimizer so updates must satisfy them.
concepts.title: Natural-Language Optimizer Constraints

concepts.description: A middleware warning appended after tool output routinely gets ignored on the very next model turn — promote it into a top-of-context reminder before that turn instead of trailing it after the observation.
concepts.title: Next-Turn Salience Promotion

concepts.description: Not every workflow task needs an LLM — mechanical, retrieval, and classification tasks are usually cheaper and more dependable without one.
concepts.title: Non-LLM Task Implementation

concepts.description: Test new prompt or harness ideas against a simulated success signal before exposing them to real users, since there is no live feedback signal offline.
concepts.title: Offline Evaluation Proxies

concepts.description: Run 5–20 representative inputs through prompt assembly, save prompts and completions, and eyeball diffs — the first offline harness before automated scoring.
concepts.title: Offline Example Suites

concepts.description: Prototype and score prompt or task changes against proxies or LLM judges before shipping, exercising as much of the real feedforward path as possible.
concepts.title: Offline Prompt Evaluation

concepts.description: A short role string on each optimizable variable steers what textual-gradient descent is allowed to rewrite — answer-only vs reasoning-plus-answer, and more.
concepts.title: Optimization Variable Role Description

concepts.description: Show the textual optimizer worked examples of desired variable properties so rewrites match target style, format, or quality traits.
concepts.title: Optimizer In-Context Examples

concepts.description: Treat the context window like RAM and external stores like disk so a finite window can page facts in and out under agent or harness control.
concepts.title: OS-Inspired Agent Memory

concepts.description: Grade what the agent produced or achieved, not the specific tool-call sequence it followed to get there — and give multi-step tasks a continuum of credit instead of one binary pass/fail.
concepts.title: Outcome-Based Partial-Credit Grading

concepts.description: Because generation is probabilistic, the same or a near-identical prompt can yield meaningfully different completions across calls — a property to manage, not a bug to eliminate.
concepts.title: Output Consistency and Robustness

concepts.description: A completion is text by default, but transforming it into the right output medium — speech, a UI event, a diff — is part of closing the application loop.
concepts.title: Output Medium Transformation

concepts.description: Improve hard tasks by eliciting intermediate tokens before the final answer — orthogonal to input-side tricks like instructions, few-shots, or soft prompts.
concepts.title: Output-Side Reasoning Augmentation

concepts.description: Two opposite ways to summarize an agent's per-trial success rate across k attempts — pass@k asks whether at least one attempt succeeds, pass^k asks whether all of them do — and they tell opposite stories as k grows.
concepts.title: Pass@k and Pass^k

concepts.description: Classify an applied-but-unresolved code patch by which of the fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass test sets it satisfies — not every non-fix is the same failure.
concepts.title: Patch Outcome Taxonomy

concepts.description: Fine-tune a model to emit meaningless filler tokens before answering, giving it extra timesteps to incorporate context before committing to output.
concepts.title: Pause Tokens

concepts.description: Collect task I/O examples and run offline prompt harnesses so each workflow step can change safely without regressing expected completions.
concepts.title: Per-Task Offline Harness Tests

concepts.description: Drop the lowest-perplexity tokens from a prompt using a small reference model, trading human readability for compression ratio since only the target LLM, not a person, needs to parse the result.
concepts.title: Perplexity-Based Prompt Compression

concepts.description: For a long-running autonomous exploration task, mandate a checkpointed partial write well before completion and periodic updates after — so a useful artifact exists even if the run is cut off early.
concepts.title: Phased Explore-Write-Early Pattern

concepts.description: Prompt the model to form an overarching plan before working the problem step by step, without any tool use or think-act-observe loop.
concepts.title: Plan-and-Solve Prompting

concepts.description: Decouple plan generation from execution so a bad plan can be rejected before it burns tool calls, tokens, and irreversible side effects.
concepts.title: Plan Validate Execute

concepts.description: Choose what a generated answer gets compared against as carefully as the comparison procedure itself — a mismatched baseline makes the result look objective while actually measuring something else.
concepts.title: Preference-Comparison Baseline Selection

concepts.description: Grow from a bare model API to a full agentic system in ordered steps — context, guardrails, routing/gateway, caching, then write-capable loops.
concepts.title: Progressive Agent Architecture

concepts.description: A working prompt usually combines a task description, optional examples, and the concrete task, with placement tuned per model.
concepts.title: Prompt Anatomy

concepts.description: Assembling a final prompt is an optimization problem — pick the highest-value elements that fit the token budget and respect dependencies.
concepts.title: Prompt Assembly Algorithms

concepts.description: Version prompts independently of application code with metadata so shared prompts can be pinned, searched, and evolved without silent force-updates.
concepts.title: Prompt Catalog

concepts.description: Give a prompt's instruction and question a light compression ratio and its demonstrations a heavier one, selecting which demonstrations survive by perplexity rather than compressing every segment uniformly.
concepts.title: Prompt Compression Budget Allocation

concepts.description: Four conditions a prompt must satisfy at once to turn a user's problem into a completion that actually solves it.
concepts.title: Prompt Conversion Criteria

concepts.description: Some prompt elements require another element already be present, and some exclude each other, both of which prompt assembly must be able to express.
concepts.title: Prompt Element Dependency

concepts.description: Rank how crucial each prompt element is to include, separately from its position, using either a numerical score or discrete priority tiers.
concepts.title: Prompt Element Importance

concepts.description: Where a prompt element appears matters — most elements need a specific order, even though skipping an element outright is usually harmless.
concepts.title: Prompt Element Position

concepts.description: Treat the model-facing transcript as a script you author — roles, injected turns, and tools — distinct from the human’s visible conversation.
concepts.title: Prompt Engineer as Playwright

concepts.description: Crafting instructions that elicit a desired model outcome without changing weights — the first adaptation lever before heavier techniques like finetuning.
concepts.title: Prompt Engineering

concepts.description: The visible user-assistant conversation and the actual model transcript differ — the transcript is a script with several collaborating authors.
concepts.title: Prompt Engineering Playwright Metaphor

concepts.description: Rank LLM apps from thin wrappers through context injection and tools up to goal-directed agency — each level adds harness obligations, not just wording.
concepts.title: Prompt Engineering Sophistication Levels

concepts.description: Attacks that trick a model into revealing its system prompt or privileged context so an application can be replicated or exploited.
concepts.title: Prompt Extraction

concepts.description: Open a prompt by stating what kind of document it is so the model interprets everything that follows through the right lens from the first token.
concepts.title: Prompt Introduction

concepts.description: Explicit refuse rules, reinforced system instructions, and known-attack preemption inside the prompt — useful layers that never guarantee obedience.
concepts.title: Prompt-Level Attack Defenses

concepts.description: Echo prompt-token logprobs to flag anomalies (typos, odd spans) and high-information passages — thresholds must tolerate model and position drift.
concepts.title: Prompt Logprob Critical Points

concepts.description: Automated search and AI-assisted rewriting can explore the prompt space, but multiply API calls and hide template mistakes unless you inspect outputs.
concepts.title: Prompt Optimization Tooling

concepts.description: End a prompt by firmly pivoting from explaining the problem to solving it, so the model completes an answer instead of adding more framing.
concepts.title: Prompt Transition

concepts.description: Expand compact intermediate expressions into flat outputs with a few-shot rewrite prompt when you lack — or prefer not to run — a dedicated executor.
concepts.title: Prompted IR Expansion

concepts.description: Narrow model choice by picking a provider first, then capability tier, then model size within that provider's lineup — hosted API or self-hosted.
concepts.title: Provider Selection Guidance

concepts.description: An agent closes a task on a self-invented or shallow check that resembles success — row counts, file existence, a help flag — instead of reproducing the actual evaluator's exact contract.
concepts.title: Proxy-Validation Failure Pattern

concepts.description: Once an agent's own end-state check passes, intercept later destructive commands against that verified output at the tool level so a "tidy up" pass cannot erase what was just proven correct.
concepts.title: Publish-State Protection Guard

concepts.description: Place the question or lookup key both before and after long retrieved material so mid-context items can attend to the query while encoding.
concepts.title: Query-Aware Contextualization

concepts.description: Reformulate the user's latest utterance into a standalone retrieval query so ambiguous follow-ups resolve against the knowledge store correctly.
concepts.title: Query Rewriting

concepts.description: Marginalize retrieved documents once per answer sequence, or per generated token, trading single-doc coherence against multi-doc mixing.
concepts.title: RAG-Sequence vs RAG-Token

concepts.description: Interleave reasoning traces that update context without side effects and environment actions so plans stay grounded and exceptions stay recoverable.
concepts.title: ReAct Loop

concepts.description: Audit interleaved reason–act trajectories as true/false positives plus reasoning, search, hallucination, and label-ambiguity failures — not only EM.
concepts.title: ReAct Success and Failure Taxonomy

concepts.description: Let humans correct a few reasoning traces mid-episode so later actions realign — cheaper than retyping action sequences or retraining the policy.
concepts.title: ReAct Thought Editing

concepts.description: Zero-shot CoT accuracy swings widely with the exact reasoning cue — instructive triggers help; misleading or irrelevant ones collapse to baseline or worse.
concepts.title: Reasoning Trigger Sensitivity

concepts.description: Reliably extracting the answer from a completion needs a known start marker and a known end marker specific to the document format being generated.
concepts.title: Recognizable Completion Boundaries

concepts.description: Reflection evaluates feasibility, plans, and outcomes; error correction acts on that insight by regenerating plans or retries until the goal is met.
concepts.title: Reflection and Error Correction

concepts.description: Periodically synthesize recent memories into higher-level insights that cite evidence, forming trees from raw observations up to abstract self-models.
concepts.title: Reflection Tree

concepts.description: Separate an Actor, Evaluator, and Self-Reflection module so sparse outcome signals become verbal lessons that condition the next trial.
concepts.title: Reflexion

concepts.description: Sample n candidate completions from a base policy and pick the highest-scoring one under a reward or judge model — more inference compute, no extra training.
concepts.title: Rejection Sampling Best-of-N

concepts.description: Score a research agent's output on groundedness, coverage, and source quality together, since no single check like unit tests exists for open-ended synthesis.
concepts.title: Research Agent Eval Groundedness

concepts.description: Exact or semantic reuse of prior model or retrieval results to cut latency and cost — with eviction, cacheability rules, and cross-user leak vigilance.
concepts.title: Response Caching

concepts.description: Retrieve the most relevant external knowledge per query and feed it to the generator — context construction that treats the retriever as an agent tool.
concepts.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation

concepts.description: Build a retrieval query directly from the user's text, via an LLM-generated rewrite, or by letting the model decide when and what to search at all.
concepts.title: Retrieval Query Construction Spectrum

concepts.description: Split a dense (or hybrid) retriever from a seq2seq generator, with optional query-encoder finetuning while keeping the document index fixed.
concepts.title: Retriever Generator Architecture

concepts.description: Assemble agents with distinct roles, goals, and tools and delegate work between them like a team, following the AutoGen and CrewAI frameworks.
concepts.title: Role-Based Agent Delegation

concepts.description: Wrap agent search queries so strings that look like CLI flags (e.g. --notes) are never parsed as options by underlying grep/find tools.
concepts.title: Safe Search Argument Passing

concepts.description: State the goal at both the start and the end of a long prompt so a refocus after intervening context restores precise operational intent.
concepts.title: Sandwich Technique

concepts.description: Useful chain-of-thought reasoning emerges only past a model-scale threshold and often hurts smaller models — do not extrapolate from tiny-model ablations.
concepts.title: Scale-Dependent Chain of Thought

concepts.description: Prefer dropping low-value tokens over asking a model to rewrite a prompt shorter — generation-based compression can't hit a target ratio reliably, costs more, and tends to lose the reasoning path.
concepts.title: Selection-Based vs Generation-Based Prompt Compression

concepts.description: Sample multiple independent CoT reasoning paths and marginalize to the most consistent final answer — a self-ensemble without a trained verifier.
concepts.title: Self-Consistency Decoding

concepts.description: Ask the model to check its own output for errors before accepting it, as a lightweight reflection step inside a single generation or agent turn.
concepts.title: Self-Critique Prompting

concepts.description: Let the agent call memory tools itself — guided by hierarchy docs and pressure signals — rather than only a fixed external eviction policy.
concepts.title: Self-Directed Memory Management

concepts.description: Let a code agent write and run its own unit-test suite so sparse pass/fail signals ground reflection without an external oracle — enabling pass@1 loops.
concepts.title: Self-Generated Test Evaluator

concepts.description: Scope a harness-editing agent's write access to the harness workspace alone so every measured gain is attributable to a harness edit, not a disabled check or a swapped model.
concepts.title: Self-Modifying Harness Controllability

concepts.description: Sample candidate API calls, execute them, keep only those that reduce future token loss, then finetune so the model learns when tools help.
concepts.title: Self-Supervised Tool Annotation

concepts.description: Classification labels that share a starting token have their probabilities compound at that token, which can make a worse option outrank a better one.
concepts.title: Shared Token Prefix Trap

concepts.description: A fix that only patches the first matching occurrence of a duplicated pattern can pass the target test yet regress the sibling occurrences it never touched.
concepts.title: Single-Site Edit Blind Spot

concepts.description: Persist newly composed skills that proved useful so later tasks can reuse them as first-class tools instead of rediscovering the composition.
concepts.title: Skill Library

concepts.description: Format a retrieved data snippet to match the prompt's document type — conversation turn, report section, or serialized structure.
concepts.title: Snippet Formatting by Document Type

concepts.description: A well-formatted prompt snippet is modular, natural in its document, brief, and inert — its token count doesn't shift when neighboring text changes.
concepts.title: Snippet Formatting Goals

concepts.description: Grade free-form completions with Specific questions, Ordinal scales, and Multi-Aspect criteria — as a third-party judge, validated against humans.
concepts.title: SOMA LLM Assessment

concepts.description: A model extrapolates whatever pattern its few-shot examples happen to exhibit, including accidental ones like ordering, not just the intended one.
concepts.title: Spurious Pattern Extrapolation

concepts.description: Give the agent a windowed, line-numbered view of the open file with goto and scroll commands instead of flooding context with full-file dumps.
concepts.title: Stateful File Viewer

concepts.description: Give a conversation a persistent object that gets edited in place across turns, instead of having the model re-emit a fresh copy into the transcript every time.
concepts.title: Stateful Object of Discourse

concepts.description: Bind an agent permanently to one work item instead of restarting fresh each time, so it can track that item's state and notify dependents when it changes.
concepts.title: Stateful Task Agents

concepts.description: Split always-on task clarification from per-instance context so instructions stay consistent while dynamic material can change every call.
concepts.title: Static vs Dynamic Prompt Content

concepts.description: Halt generation at known end markers server-side (or cancel a stream) so postscripts never burn tokens after the extractable answer is complete.
concepts.title: Stop Sequences

concepts.description: Optimize prompts for a cheaper inference model with feedback from a stronger model so you pay a fixed optimization cost and keep inference cheap.
concepts.title: Strong-to-Weak Prompt Optimization

concepts.description: Store tables, queues, and other structured state outside raw prompt text so the agent can rely on shape the context window alone cannot preserve.
concepts.title: Structured Agent Memory

concepts.description: Write a prompt as a formally specified document — XML, YAML, or JSON — to make strong assumptions about completion shape and ease parsing.
concepts.title: Structured Document Format

concepts.description: Guaranteeing a completion parses into a required schema needs one of four techniques, each with a different reliability-versus-effort tradeoff.
concepts.title: Structured Output Generation

concepts.description: A model can't examine or manipulate individual letters within its own tokens, so any task requiring that should be handled outside the LLM.
concepts.title: Subtoken Task Avoidance

concepts.description: A cost-normalized accuracy metric — expected task successes per million tokens spent — for comparing harness configurations that trade accuracy against token cost.
concepts.title: Successes Per Million Tokens

concepts.description: Split developer instructions into a privileged system prompt and user content into a user prompt, then render them through the model's chat template.
concepts.title: System Prompt Architecture

concepts.description: Answer structured-data questions via text-to-SQL, execution, and generation — treating schema selection and SQL runners as agent tools.
concepts.title: Tabular Retrieval Tools

concepts.description: Split a complex job into chained simpler prompts for better control, cheaper models on easy steps, and inspectable intermediate outputs.
concepts.title: Task Decomposition Prompting

concepts.description: Define each workflow task's input/output shape explicitly, and separately keep a clear-enough idea of how the task should be accomplished.
concepts.title: Task I/O Schema Design

concepts.description: When a task's first-draft results aren't good enough, escalate through a fixed sequence of fixes rather than reaching for the most complex one first.
concepts.title: Task Quality Escalation Ladder

concepts.description: Summarize source text for a fixed downstream question so retained details match the later prompt — trading reusability for relevance.
concepts.title: Task-Specific Summarization

concepts.description: A model computes a full probability distribution over the next token, and sampling — controlled by temperature — decides how faithfully generation follows versus deviates from the single most likely choice.
concepts.title: Temperature and Sampling

concepts.description: Implement a workflow task as a prompt template that fills inputs, elicits a completion, and post-processes the text into the task's output schema.
concepts.title: Templated Prompt Task

concepts.description: Self-written evaluator tests bound reflection quality: false positives cause premature wrong submits; false negatives are safer because bad tests can be spotted.
concepts.title: Test Suite Fidelity

concepts.description: Treat candidate code as an instance-optimization variable scored by local tests plus an LLM evaluator that critiques failures without rewriting code.
concepts.title: Test-Time Code Refinement

concepts.description: Generate several candidate completions instead of one and select the best, trading roughly linear extra cost for higher output quality.
concepts.title: Test-Time Compute Sampling

concepts.description: At inference, treat the current answer as an optimizable variable and iterate self-supervised LLM critiques via textual gradient descent before committing.
concepts.title: Test-Time Solution Refinement

concepts.description: Update a graph variable by asking an LLM to incorporate textual-gradient criticisms — the natural-language analogue of an SGD step.
concepts.title: Textual Gradient Descent

concepts.description: Natural-language criticisms of a variable’s role in a computation graph, produced by an LLM as the analogue of a numerical gradient.
concepts.title: Textual Gradients

concepts.description: Keep a window of past variable values in the optimizer context so updates see trajectory history, not only the latest textual gradients.
concepts.title: Textual Optimizer Momentum

concepts.description: Tokenizing two concatenated strings together can yield a different token count than tokenizing them separately, so token budgets aren't additive.
concepts.title: Token Boundary Inertness

concepts.description: Let find/quote tools match case-insensitively and return abbreviated start–end spans so evidence fits the context budget without full-page dumps.
concepts.title: Token-Efficient Quote Observations

concepts.description: LLMs process text as deterministic multicharacter tokens, not letters, which makes token count — not character count — the real unit of prompt length.
concepts.title: Tokenization Fundamentals

concepts.description: Control how freely the model may emit tool-call tokens at decode time — too tight under-calls, too loose destroys calibration of when tools help.
concepts.title: Tool Call Decoding Budget

concepts.description: Surface an agent's background tool activity in the chat UI itself so users can inspect the rationale behind an unexpected response.
concepts.title: Tool-Call Transparency UI

concepts.description: Name, schema, and documentation choices that make tools easy for the model to select and call correctly without overlapping or over-complex surfaces.
concepts.title: Tool Definition Design

concepts.description: Native function calling is a fine-tuned chat model plus API-level syntactic sugar — tool defs render as TypeScript signatures, calls as ChatML-like tags.
concepts.title: Tool Definition Internal Representation

concepts.description: The declared set of tools an agent may call; inventory size is a capability versus reliability and context-budget tradeoff.
concepts.title: Tool Inventory

concepts.description: Empirically size and prune an agent's tool inventory by measuring performance with and without each tool and replacing chronically misused ones.
concepts.title: Tool Selection Ablation

concepts.description: Train an LM to choose which API to call, when, with what arguments, and how to use the result — self-supervised, without tying tools to one task.
concepts.title: Toolformer Tool Use

concepts.description: Drop prior conversation once the topic has moved on, using an inactivity threshold or a relevance-judging model to detect the shift.
concepts.title: Topic-Shift Context Truncation

concepts.description: Choose how a completion model's conversation transcript is written on the page — freeform, script-style, markerless, or structured tags.
concepts.title: Transcript Format Selection

concepts.description: Deliberate inference that searches a tree of coherent intermediate thoughts with LM generation, evaluation, lookahead, and backtracking.
concepts.title: Tree of Thoughts

concepts.description: A model presented with a false premise tends to continue assuming it's true rather than self-correcting, because self-correcting documents are rare in training data.
concepts.title: Truth Bias

concepts.description: First prompt for a reasoning trace, then a second self-augmented prompt that appends an answer-format trigger and parses the final answer.
concepts.title: Two-Stage Reasoning–Answer Extraction

concepts.description: Scope an LLM application by four independent axes — medium, abstraction level, context required, and statefulness — before designing the harness.
concepts.title: User Problem Domain Complexity
